item.title: The New Sociology of Propaganda
item.content:encoded:
Freeden Blume Oeur, Tufts University

Fiona Greenland, University of Virginia

Propaganda remains a significant social problem in contemporary society, shaped by proliferating media and competing actors seeking to control narratives. The landscape has evolved from earlier historical periods to encompass AI-generated content, digital platforms, and novel forms of misinformation.

This special issue seeks sociological research examining modern propaganda across all methodologies. The call invites empirical, historical, and theoretical contributions exploring how propaganda operates, who creates and targets it, its role in contemporary conflicts, and how communities resist or utilize it. Research should illuminate propaganda's relationships with power dynamics, censorship, radicalization, and information manipulation.

Appel publié par British Journal of Sociology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Modern propaganda operation and social consequences
  • Power and propaganda in systems of oppression
  • Machinery of modern propaganda
  • Propaganda actors and targets
  • Propaganda in conflicts and crises
  • Resistance and confrontation of propaganda
  • Propaganda in everyday lives
  • Propaganda and related topics
  • Propaganda spread across communities and borders
  • Detecting and avoiding propaganda harms
